anxiety_info.title: Why does anxiety happen, and why won't it go away?
anxiety_info.description: Anxiety isn't your enemy—it's a signal from your mind, trying to keep you safe.

step1.title: Anxiety is a survival alarm
content: Since ancient times, anxiety has been a built-in alarm protecting us from danger.
It's your brain's instinctive way of shouting, "Watch out!"
Feeling anxious simply means your survival instinct is still working.

step2.title: It comes and goes like waves
content: Anxiety doesn't stay in your heart forever.
Like ocean waves, it slowly rises, swells, and gently fades again.
It might feel endless right now, but every wave is bound to pass.

step3.title: Waves are a natural part of the ocean
content: The ocean always has waves, big and small.
Having waves doesn't mean anything is wrong with the ocean.
Our minds are the same—anxiety isn't a flaw to fix, but a natural movement.

step4.title: Acknowledge the wave as it arrives
content: In modern life, anxiety often shows up even when there's no real danger.
Instead of forcing it down, try acknowledging that a wave is rising in your heart.
Gently say to yourself, "I see that I'm feeling tense right now."

step5.title: Moving forward with anxiety
content: You don't need to wait for the waves to stop.
Just as the deep ocean keeps its course even when the surface is rough,
you can carry your anxiety and still move toward the life you want.

act_guide.title: Moving Forward with Anxiety
act_guide.description: Instead of fighting anxiety, learn about ACT—a way to move toward the life you want, even with anxiety along for the ride.

step1.title: What is ACT?
content: ACT (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy) helps you accept anxiety as it is,
rather than suppressing it, and commit to acting on the values you care about.
Our app breaks this into 5 steps you can easily follow.

step2.title: Surfacing to the present moment
content: When caught in a spiral of thoughts, try Step 1 (Grounding) and Step 2 (Emotion Diary).
By tuning into your senses and calmly noting your inner weather,
you can find a calm center even amidst the roughest waves.

step3.title: Separating thoughts from facts
content: Step 3 helps you see thoughts like "I'm going to fail" from a distance.
It's a practice of noticing that a thought is just a thought—like wind on the surface.
Thoughts are passing breezes, not the truth of the ocean.

step4.title: Breathing with the rhythm of the waves
content: In Step 4 (Accepting Anxiety), breathe along with the rising and falling wave animation.
Instead of pushing anxiety away, make room for it within you.
As you breathe in and out, let the wave simply flow through.

step5.title: Moving toward your own values
content: In the final step, discover what you truly value and take action.
Even when anxious, you can still take small steps toward what matters.
Start with one small thing you can do today, waves and all.
